scenes.heading: Exterior angles
scenes.sub: Every polygon turns you a full circle
scenes.say: A robot tracing a shape doesn't care about the angles inside the corners. It cares how far to turn. Those turns are exterior angles, and they follow one amazing rule.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Walk around a park and turn at every corner
scenes.science: The exterior angles of any convex polygon add to 360°
scenes.breaks: it needs every turn to go the same way. A corner pointing inwards makes you turn back the other way.
scenes.say: Imagine walking around a park shaped like a polygon, turning left at each corner. Back at the start, you face the same way again. You've turned one full circle, three hundred and sixty degrees, however many corners there are.

scenes.heading: Interior and exterior angles
notes: Extend one side past the corner
scenes.say: First the pentagon, then one side extended past corner C. The exterior angle e is the turn at that corner. It sits on a straight line with the interior angle i.

scenes.heading: Two key facts
points: The 360° doesn't depend on the sides
scenes.say: So interior plus exterior is one hundred and eighty at every corner. And the exterior angles of a convex polygon always add to three hundred and sixty degrees.

scenes.heading: All the turns together
notes: Extend every side the same way round
scenes.say: Now extend every side, going the same way around the shape. The four turns, a, b, c and d, make one full turn: three hundred and sixty degrees.
scenes.caption: Extend every side, going the same way around. The four turns a, b, c and d make one full turn: 360°.

scenes.heading: Regular polygons
scenes.say: In a regular polygon, all n exterior angles are equal, so each one is three hundred and sixty divided by n. Turn it around to find n: three hundred and sixty divided by the exterior angle. Then the interior angle is one hundred and eighty minus the exterior angle.
scenes.caption: In a regular polygon, each exterior angle is 360 ÷ n. Turned around: n = 360 ÷ exterior. Then interior = 180 − exterior.

scenes.heading: Regular octagon
scenes.question: Find each exterior and interior angle of a regular octagon.
scenes.say: A regular octagon has eight equal turns. Three hundred and sixty divided by eight is forty-five degrees. So each interior angle is one hundred and eighty minus forty-five: one hundred and thirty-five degrees. That's quicker than the angle sum method!
scenes.caption: 8 equal turns: 360 ÷ 8 = 45°. So each interior angle is 180 − 45 = 135°. Quicker than the angle sum method!

scenes.heading: How many sides?
scenes.question: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 140°. How many sides does it have?
scenes.say: Each interior angle is one hundred and forty. Don't divide three hundred and sixty by that! First change it to the exterior angle: one hundred and eighty minus one hundred and forty is forty. Then three hundred and sixty divided by forty is nine. It has nine sides.
scenes.caption: Don't divide 360 by the interior angle! First change to exterior: 180 − 140 = 40°. Then 360 ÷ 40 = 9 sides.

scenes.say: Quick recap. Walk the park, turn a circle: exterior angles add to three hundred and sixty. Interior plus exterior is one hundred and eighty. For a regular polygon, the exterior angle is three hundred and sixty over n, and n is three hundred and sixty over the exterior angle. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Walk the park, turn a circle: exterior angles add to 360°. Interior + exterior = 180°. Regular polygon: exterior = 360 ÷ n, and n = 360 ÷ exterior. Now try the practice questions!
